Container.Name: epd-remote
Container.Overview:
Remote management tool for e-ink (EPD) displays: the frontend generates and previews the image to send, the backend connects to the display over Bluetooth (BLE) and pushes the data. Bluetooth requires the host network (AF_BLUETOOTH sockets are isolated per network namespace, and hci0 lives in the host's netns), so this template is fixed to Network Type=Host and cannot be switched to bridge networking. The host does not need BlueZ installed: the container starts its own dbus-daemon and bluetoothd to manage the adapter. It only needs the host to recognize the Bluetooth hardware (USB or built-in) — check with `ls /sys/class/bluetooth` for hci0.
Source and builds live in the dongshuzhao/epd-remote project on Docker Hub; this template pulls dongshuzhao/epd-remote:latest directly, no local docker build needed.
Container.Requires: The host needs a usable Bluetooth adapter (USB or built-in), and no other process should be holding hci0 (e.g. a bluetoothd already running on the host). The image is published on Docker Hub as dongshuzhao/epd-remote and will be pulled automatically on install — no local build required.

Config.Name: AppData Directory
Config.Description: Storage for remembered devices and send history

Config.Name: EPD_PORT
Config.Description: Web UI port (avoid clashing with other containers since this uses host networking)

Config.Name: EPD_DATA_DIR
Config.Description: Data directory inside the container, paired with the AppData Directory mount above; usually leave as-is

Config.Name: EPD_START_BLUETOOTHD
Config.Description: 1 = the container starts its own dbus-daemon+bluetoothd (use this on hosts without BlueZ, e.g. Unraid). If the host already runs bluetoothd, mount /run/dbus instead and set EPD_USE_HOST_DBUS=1 — don't enable both

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Timezone, used for the timestamp sent to the display by the time-sync feature
